title: Get a DOM node with a ref

slides.say: Sometimes you need the real DOM element, to focus an input or scroll to it. Refs do that.
Create a ref with null. Pass it as the ref attribute. React puts the DOM node into ref dot current, and you can call browser APIs like focus.

slides.text: Starts as null. Set during commit. Back to null when removed.
slides.say: It starts as null. React fills it in when it creates the node, and sets it back to null when the node is removed.

slides.text: Best for focus, scroll and measuring.
slides.say: Use it for non destructive things: focusing, scrolling, and measuring.
